text: Yes, tree-cover loss occurred on this 58.1-hectare rural asset in 2023, totaling 0.7 hectares, or 1.2% of the asset. The evidence shows that the area was forested in 2020 and that the loss was detected by multiple independent sources (Hansen Global Forest Change and JRC Global Forest Cover 2020). The affected area was primarily planted forest (Eucalyptus grandis), not native forest. However, the evidence does not confirm whether the loss was due to deforestation, as it could reflect legal harvesting, natural disturbance, or other stand-replacement activities.
